html:
Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1520 to 1566, the longest reign in its history and the peak of its power. Europeans called him the Magnificent; Turks call him Kanuni, "the Lawgiver".

He took Belgrade in 1521 and the island fortress of Rhodes in the siege of Rhodes in 1522. In 1526 he crushed the Hungarian army at the Battle of Mohács, and in 1529 he laid siege to Vienna but failed to take it. In the east he took Baghdad and Iraq from Safavid Iran in 1534. His admiral Hayreddin Barbarossa made the Ottoman navy the strongest in the Mediterranean.

At home he issued law codes that set out taxes, land rights and punishments alongside Islamic law. He broke custom by marrying Hurrem Sultan, a former slave from Ruthenia, who became a powerful voice at court. He later had his eldest son Mustafa executed. His architect Mimar Sinan built him the Süleymaniye Mosque. He died in 1566 in his tent during a siege in Hungary.
